title: Improved Sample Complexity of Robust Reinforcement Learning with KL Uncertainty Sets
claim: Matching upper and lower bounds across uncertainty levels show how complexity changes by regime, closing the gap left by prior results.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, one per parameter regime, shared axes
description: Three side-by-side schematic line plots, labeled (a), (b) and (c). Each is a different regime of the minimum transition probability p∧, and the regimes are given as inequalities under the panels. Each plot has uncertainty level δ on the x-axis and sample complexity on the y-axis, with tick labels written as math expressions. A solid blue line is the upper bound and a dashed orange line is the lower bound. A green horizontal line marks a prior upper bound from Li et al., 2025. The blue and orange curves rise piecewise, then merge into one exponential-looking curve that meets the green line near log(1/p∧). A separate flat segment on the right is labeled the worst-path regime. Small arrows point to formulas on the curves. Dashed vertical grid lines mark the breakpoints. The eye goes first to the blue and orange curves against the green ceiling.
caption: Illustrations of the obtained sample complexity upper and lower bounds under KL-defined uncertainty sets
abstract: In this paper, we study distributionally robust reinforcement learning with Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence-defined uncertainty sets. The goal is to find a policy that maximizes the robust value function, defined as the worst-case value over all transition kernels in the uncertainty set. Assuming access to a generative model, we aim to understand the sample complexity of finding an $Îµ$-optimal robust policy. The best-known sample complexity results in the literature show a non-trivial gap of $\mathcal{O}\{\max\{p_\wedge^{-1}(1-Î³)^{-1},(1-Î³)^{-2}\}\}$ between the upper and lower bounds, where $p_\wedge$ denotes the minimum positive transition probability of the nominal transition kernel, and $Î³$ is the discount factor. More importantly, existing results on the lower bound only cover a limited range of the uncertainty level. In this paper, we develop tighter and complete upper and lower bounds for robust RL with KL-defined uncertainty sets. Our upper bound is the tightest among all existing studies, and it improves upon the best-known bound by at least the order of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{p_\wedge^{-1},(1-Î³)^{-1}\})$ for uncertainty level $Î´\in(0,1)$. Furthermore, our lower bound holds for any uncertainty level. Our upper and lower bounds (nearly) match in various regimes, providing improved results for this problem.
